keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row). The infobox: 'Territory controlled by the Philippine Republic, most of which it occupied except Manila and parts of Mindanao', area '1898: 298,719 km2' (flagged 'better source needed'). That figure is the whole archipelago (the grid's Philippines is 266,300 km2, ratio 0.89); the shape here (country minus Manila minus Mindanao, 180,800 km2 of grid cells, ratio 0.61 against the infobox) is within a factor of two of the infobox, though the page says only 'parts of Mindanao'.

After the fall of Malolos (31 March 1899) the republic's seats moved north: Bayombong (Nueva Vizcaya) from November 1899, Lubuagan (Kalinga) from 6 March to 18 May 1900, Palanan (Isabela) until 23 March 1901. The page gives no territory for 1900-1901; the three provinces are the researcher's reading of the capitals (a guerrilla republic holding no continuous area).

ledger.note: 12 June 1898: Aguinaldo declares independence. 'On June 12, he issued the Philippine Declaration of Independence from Spain at his ancestral home in Cavite'; the preceding government was the Revolutionary Government of the Philippines; the Republic itself was proclaimed on 23 January 1899. The page gives no territory for June 1898; the archipelago minus Manila and Mindanao is the infobox's description of what it later occupied.
23 January 1899: the Revolutionary Government becomes the First Philippine Republic (Malolos Republic). Infobox 'Republic proclaimed: January 23, 1899'; capital Malolos.

region.text: Manila and its surroundings, where the fighting erupted

ledger.note: 4 February 1899: the Philippine-American War begins. 'On February 4, fighting erupted in Manila between American and Filipino forces.' The treaty of Paris (10 December 1898) had transferred Spain's claim to the United States.

31 March 1899: Malolos falls. 'On March 31, American forces captured Malolos, the initial seat of the Philippine Republic government.' The capital moved to Angeles from 17 March and to San Isidro on 29 March; the province of Bulacan, in which Malolos lies, is the researcher's reading of the town.

ledger.note: 1900: the republic shrinks to northern Luzon. Between the fall of Malolos (31 March 1899) and the capital at Lubuagan (6 March 1900) the page gives no further dated loss; the difference between the 1898-1899 shape and the three northern provinces is a bridge.

19 April 1901: the republic is dissolved de jure. 'Palanan, Isabela - On March 23, 1901, General Aguinaldo was captured by American forces'; 'Following his capture, Aguinaldo announced allegiance to the United States on April 19, 1901' (infobox 'De jure dissolution: 19 April 1901', 'De facto dissolution: 16 April 1902'; one footnote gives the oath as 1 April, another source as 2 April).

notes: Written 2026-10-24 by the se-03-x additions batch, from the first-philippine-republic suggestions in the am-06-b and am-07-c reports; the spanish-east-indies and united-states-of-america dossiers already name this slug. One page opened. Unsettled: (1) the page gives no territory by province: 'parts of Mindanao' are not named, so the whole of Mindanao is removed, and the area ratio compares an infobox that equals the whole archipelago; (2) the start: the Republic was proclaimed on 23 January 1899, the dossier starts with the independence declaration of 12 June 1898 (the Revolutionary Government), since the Spanish East Indies dossier hands the land to this slug; (3) the capitals 1899: the page lists Bayombong from November 1899 and Bayambang until 13 November 1899 without ordering them; the republic was never at Bacoor or Kawit in the page's list; (4) the oath of allegiance: 1 April 1901 (footnote), 2 April 1901 (Beede), 19 April 1901 (text and infobox de jure); the dossier follows 19 April; (5) the 1900 loss is a bridge (confidence 1), and the northern provinces of 1900-1901 are read from the capitals; (6) the Visayas and Mindanao parts of the republic (Panay, Negros, Cebu, Misamis) are not on the page; (7) the US dossier ends its contest on 19 April 1901 against this slug, as here; (8) type rebel for an unrecognised republic that held land and was crushed. Gazetteer: Malolos, Kawit, Bayombong, Lubuagan, Palanan, Bayambang, Bamban, San Isidro.
